title: Functions: Basics
description: Domain and range, composition, inverse functions, symmetry and monotonicity.
html:
📈 Functions: Basics

1. The function concept

A function $f \colon D \to \mathbb{R}$ assigns to each $x \in D$ exactly one value $f(x)$. Vertical line test: every vertical line meets the graph at most once.

Domain

$$\tfrac{1}{g(x)}: g(x) \neq 0, \qquad \sqrt{g(x)}: g(x) \ge 0, \qquad \ln g(x): g(x) > 0$$

Range: all values actually attained, e.g. $x^2 + 1$ has $W = [1, \infty)$.

2. Composition

$$(f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x)), \qquad f \circ g \neq g \circ f$$

$f(x) = x^2$, $g(x) = x + 1$: $(f \circ g)(x) = (x + 1)^2$, $(g \circ f)(x) = x^2 + 1$.

3. Inverse function

Solve $y = f(x)$ for $x$, swap names. Exists only for injective $f$ (horizontal line test). The graph of $f^{-1}$ is the reflection in $y = x$.

$$f(x) = x^2 \ (x \ge 0) \Rightarrow f^{-1}(x) = \sqrt{x}, \qquad f(x) = 2x + 3 \Rightarrow f^{-1}(x) = \tfrac{x - 3}{2}$$

4. Symmetry and monotonicity

  • even: $f(-x) = f(x)$ (symmetric about the $y$-axis), e.g. $x^2$, $|x|$, $\cos x$
  • odd: $f(-x) = -f(x)$ (symmetric about the origin), e.g. $x^3$, $\sin x$
  • strictly increasing: $x_1 < x_2 \Rightarrow f(x_1) < f(x_2)$

5. Transformations

$$g(x) = a \cdot f(x - d) + e$$

$d$: shift to the right, $e$: upwards, $a$: stretch in $y$-direction ($a < 0$ reflects). Piecewise functions: check the seams for jumps.
